applicant_utility.summary: This is Qatar University's main award for non-Qatari first-year undergraduates: tuition and textbook exemptions plus a 500 QAR monthly salary, shared on-campus housing with transport, an annual round-trip air fare ticket and a QU-sponsored residence permit. The 95% high school average bar makes it one of the most competitive undergraduate scholarships in the Gulf, so apply but keep safer, funded options open in parallel. Timing is the trap: the international window has historically opened 1 March and closed 25 March, yet QU's current timeline page says the next intake's dates are not yet decided, so monitor the official timeline rather than assume a fixed annual date. Everything hinges on the original certified transcript physically reaching Doha by the document deadline - an online upload alone will void the file.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International high school graduates with a 95%+ average who want a fully funded bachelor's degree in Doha with tuition, housing, flights and a stipend all covered.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify your high school average meets the 95% minimum under QU's evaluation before investing in the application
Complete the QU online admission application (myBanner) including the 'Scholarship Application' section - the admission application doubles as the scholarship application
Pay the non-refundable QR 200 application fee and upload a passport-size photograph and a copy of your passport
Courier the original, certified high school transcript (with copies for checking) to the Admissions Department, Qatar University, P.O. Box 2713, Doha, Qatar well before the document deadline
Submit IELTS/TOEFL and SAT/ACT results if you have them even though they are not mandatory - the committee may weigh them when ranking competitive applicants
Plan for the Foundation Program: if your college requires it, you must pass it within two semesters or the scholarship is terminated
common_rejection_risks: A high school average below the published 95% minimum - it is an application requirement, not a guideline
The original certified transcript not reaching the Admissions Department in Doha by the document deadline; QU states the international application will not be considered without it
Applying through the wrong route - transfer, visiting, non-degree and second bachelor's degree applicants are explicitly excluded
Holding another sponsorship or scholarship at the same time, which the rules prohibit

Failing the first semester, or slipping below a 3.0 cumulative GPA or 12 credit hours per semester - for international students, termination also cancels residency sponsorship and the student is sent home on a one-way ticket
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The non-refundable QR 200 admission application fee, day-to-day personal spending beyond the 500 QAR monthly stipend, penalty fines for withdrawing from courses after the add/drop period, and any expense outside the published benefit list (for example charges around summer/winter terms, which sit outside the funded Fall/Spring semesters).
document_audit: The original certified high school transcript must physically arrive in Doha - uploads or photocopies alone do not satisfy the international applicant requirement
Transcripts must be final, official and certified, and any non-Arabic/English document needs a certified translation or it will be queried

The health certificate must be issued inside Qatar and be no more than six months old at examination - international applicants follow the International Students website process, not the in-Qatar centres
Do not file a separate self-funded student visa application when competing for this scholarship; QU issues the visa only for scholarship recipients, and mixing the two routes confuses the file
alerts: The upcoming Spring 2027 international dates are officially 'not yet determined' - QU has historically opened this window on 1 March and closed it 25 March, so check the timeline page from January onward
The scholarship must start in the semester it is awarded; a one-semester postponement is only possible with scholarship committee approval
Failing the first semester cancels the award, and under the continuity rules international recipients who lose the scholarship have their residency cancelled and are given a one-way ticket home
The award cannot be combined with any other sponsorship or scholarship, including external ones
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the online admission application with the scholarship section completed and the QR 200 fee during the announced international window, courier original certified documents to the QU Admissions Department in Doha by the document deadline, then await the initial conditional acceptance letter; once admitted, QU processes the student visa and emails the final admission and scholarship decision.
